physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the pineal gland, the small grain set deep in the middle of the head, behind the eyes, between the hemispheres. It is the body's quietest organ, and the one the old maps reached for whenever they tried to name a place where the inside of a person looks out. It is fitting. This is the code of the question that does not stop, and the gland sits exactly where the questioning is felt, at the back of the brow, behind the place where thought presses.

The shadow has a bodily floor here. When the doubt turns inward and starts gnawing, the body knows it before the mind names it. Sleep gets light. The head feels lit from inside at the wrong hours. There is a tightness at the brow, a faint clenching just above and between the eyes, that no amount of reasoning will undo. The pineal is the gland that runs the body's sense of day and night, and a self-doubting mind quietly throws that timing off. The body is keeping the score the mind is refusing to read.

The climb out is also bodily. The brow softens before the question is answered. Sleep deepens. There is a settling at the centre of the head, a sense that the asking has somewhere to go now and is no longer chewing on its own host. The inquiry can keep running. The body just stops paying for it.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the gland, this code answers to a single amino acid, Proline. Proline is the strange one in the set. It is the only amino acid whose side chain folds back and binds to its own backbone, locking itself into a ring. Where the other amino acids let the chain flow, Proline puts a bend in it. It is the kink, the turn, the place where a protein has to change direction.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the quiet shock of this card. The code of doubt is built on the one element in the body's alphabet that loops back on itself. The chemistry is doing what the mind does. The question that bends around to question itself, the logic that cancels its own logic, the inquiry that finally turns toward the asker, all of it is already written into the shape of this molecule. The card does not invent the move. It inherits it. The body has been folding back on itself, at every joint of every protein, all along.
